Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'token' (potions.py:373), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy. Token rarity is not in any reward or shop bucket, which potions.py:375 records as in_reward_pool = False and potion_pools.POTION_POOL records by omission. Its only source is the ported relic Petrified Toad, which procures one at the start of every combat (relics/petrified_toad.py:18-20) -- see audit/records/relic/petrified_toad.json, whose N1 already verdicts the procurement of THIS potion.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: Potion.targeted = True (potions.py:374); CombatState.use_potion resolves the enemy with CombatCtx.resolve_target (combat.py:608, 62-66) and the recording's UsePotion carries the 1-based enemy slot (conformance/combat_driver.py:288)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.AnyEnemy is the ONE value the sim's single boolean distinguishes, and `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` confirms `targeted` is True for exactly the five AnyEnemy potions and False for all 46 others. PotionModel.IsValidTarget's AnyEnemy arm (PotionModel.cs:268-271) is `target.Side != Owner.Creature.Side`, and resolve_target only ever returns a member of combat.enemies, so the guard is structurally satisfied. The dead-target arm (`!target.IsAlive` -> false, PotionModel.cs:264-267) is likewise satisfied: resolve_target falls back to the first living enemy when the indexed one is_gone.

CanonicalVars (protected override, Potio.rationale: `new DamageVar(15m, ValueProp.Unpowered)`. Checked against the C# rather than the port's docstring per PROMPT.md bug class 19; no ascension branch in the file.

OnUse (protected override, PotionShapedR.rationale: `CreatureCmd.Damage(ctx, target, base.DynamicVars.Damage, Owner.Creature, null)` -- note this call passes the DamageVar OBJECT to the overload that unpacks its value and its Props, where its siblings pass `damage.BaseValue, damage.Props` separately; same result. The sim deals 15 with NON_CARD_UNPOWERED, dealer the player, no card source (potions.py:381-387), so the 15 is blockable but not boosted by Strength or Vulnerable (cmds.py:56-58).

guards.what: N1: this potion occupies a real belt slot, so Petrified Toad's procure can push a real potion out
guards.rationale: Both sides put the rock in the first free slot and neither compacts the belt (Player.AddPotionInternal's `_potionSlots.IndexOf(null)` vs player.py:107-121), so slot IDENTITY is preserved -- which matters because a recorded UsePotion names a slot and conformance/runner.py:625-631 diffs floor_potions slot by slot. The belt-full case also agrees: the rock is silently dropped on both sides. The HOOKS the sim's procure skips are audit/records/relic/petrified_toad.json G1/G2 and are not re-verdicted here.
